entHint: Enterprise memory comes from the enterprise server and may be recalled into conversations automatically (see the switch below). You can delete items you wrote, and items in your personal collections.
entRecallLabel: Recall my enterprise memory into conversations
entNotInEnterprise: Join a project group and your available enterprise memory will show up here.
title: Memory
scopeHint: Auto-memory and project CLAUDE.md use the same folder as your Claude Code workspace. Pick a path below (or set it once here) so files match ~/.claude/projects/{sanitized}/memory and CLAUDE.md in that repo.
pickFolderUnavailable: Folder picker is only available in the desktop app.
scopeCleared: Using work directory as project root
autoHint: Files under the path below (first ~200 lines load into each Claude Code session per upstream rules).
globalHint: Path: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — instructions shared across all projects.
projectHint: Project-specific instructions; prefers .claude/CLAUDE.md, otherwise CLAUDE.md at repo root.
emptyAuto: No memory files yet — ask the model to remember something in chat, or click "Add memory".

engine.hint: The memory of One Work's built-in assistant. What you ask it to remember is saved here and read back when later conversations start.
engine.sharedHint: Read by every conversation that has no project of its own, including those started from a scene. Ask the assistant to remember something in any of them and the others will know it too.
engine.sharedEmpty: Nothing remembered yet. Ask the assistant to remember something in a conversation, or add a note here.
engine.projectsHint: The memory of a project folder you chose. Only conversations in that project read it.
engine.legacyHint: Older versions kept a separate memory for every conversation, and no other conversation could read it. {{groups}} folders with {{files}} files are still here. Merge them into the shared memory so the assistant can use them.
engine.mergeConfirm: Move these memory files into the shared memory? The originals are removed after they are copied; files with the same name but different content are kept under a new name, so nothing is lost.
engine.loadFailed: Could not read the built-in assistant memory

agents.hint: Manage the memory / instruction files that other coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode) read. Pick an agent, edit, and save.
agents.globalHint: The instruction file {{agent}} reads in every project.
agents.projectHint: The instruction file {{agent}} reads in the project folder; set the folder below.
agents.willCreate: The file does not exist yet; saving will create it

tidy.title: Tidy up the assistant's memory?
tidy.content: The assistant now remembers {{total}} items, {{mergeable}} of them older than two weeks. Too many makes it slower to look things up and uses more context. I can fold those older memories into a few files by type and month — not a word changed or dropped. A backup is taken first, and you can undo it any time in Memory.
tidy.done: Tidied: {{merged}} older memories folded into {{mergedInto}} files, every original kept. A backup was taken; undo it any time in Memory.
tidy.failed: Tidying failed; your memory was not changed
tidy.undoContent: The files from before the tidy are put back and the merged files removed. Memories saved since are kept.
tidy.undone: Undone; your memory is back as it was

space.hint: What you ask the assistant to remember is saved here automatically, so you can look it up alongside your library. This is a live view of the assistant's memory; edits take effect right away. Tidying, backups and undo are in Memory.
space.toLibraryTitle: Save this memory to the library?
space.toLibraryBody: A new document is created in My files (only you can see it) with this memory's text. The memory itself is unchanged; after that the two are edited separately.
space.toLibraryEnterprise: A new document is created in your own My files on the company server (only you can see it, not administrators) with this memory's text. The memory itself is unchanged; after that the two are edited separately.
